etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French reflexion, reflection, and its source Late Latin reflexio, from the participle stem of reflectō. The current spelling is influenced by reflect.

definitions.definition: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
The property of a propagated wave being thrown back from a surface (such as a mirror).
Something, such as an image, that is reflected.

quote.citation: 1997, In Flames (lyrics and music), “Jotun”, in Whoracle‎[1]:
quote.text: A body of black that carried no reflection.

quote.citation: 1959, Georgette Heyer, chapter 1, in The Unknown Ajax:
quote.text: But Richmond, his grandfather's darling, after one thoughtful glance cast under his lashes at that uncompromising countenance appeared to lose himself in his own reflections.

definitions.definition: (followed by on) Used to make an implied criticism.
A representative manifestation or outcome of a condition, trend or trait.

quote.citation: 2021 November 11, “When a Logo Doesn’t Risk It All: Meta’s Brand Is Designed for Unknown Worlds”, in The New York Times‎[2], archived from the original on 2023-08-04:
quote.text: Zuckerberg said last month that the name change was a reflection of how much Facebook had evolved.

definitions.definition: (computing) The process or mechanism of determining the capabilities of an object at run-time.

quote.text: DynamicMBeanFacade uses Java's reflection API to introspect the managed resource and discover data type information for attributes.

definitions.definition: (anatomy) The folding of a part; a fold.
